questions.prompt: How does Go decide whether a name is visible to other packages?

options.text: By capitalization — uppercase is exported, lowercase is private

questions.explanation: An identifier starting with an uppercase letter is exported; lowercase means unexported. Go has no visibility keywords.

questions.prompt: For a v2 or higher module, where must the major version appear?

options.text: In the module path and import path, e.g. `.../v2`
In a separate VERSION file only

questions.explanation: Because a major bump is breaking, v2+ carries the major version in the module path and imports so incompatible versions can coexist.

questions.prompt: Packages placed under an ____ directory can only be imported within the same module subtree.
questions.explanation: The `internal/` directory is enforced by the compiler: only code rooted at the same parent may import it, keeping implementation details private.

questions.prompt: What does a blank import `import _ "pkg"` do?

options.text: Imports the package only for its side effects (its init functions)
Imports it privately so it can't be used

questions.explanation: A blank import runs the package's init functions (e.g. to register a driver) without referencing it directly.

questions.prompt: Which statements about packages and modules are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: `init` runs after package variables and before `main`
Two packages may freely import each other

questions.explanation: init runs at load before main, import cycles are a compile error, and go.sum verifies dependencies. Mutual imports are not allowed.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: A directory of files sharing a package clause
Versioned packages rooted at a go.mod file
An executable program with func main()
Declares module path, Go version, dependencies

questions.explanation: A package groups files; a module versions packages; the main package is runnable; go.mod defines the module.
